bug.title: The archive backfill's rank phase is sequential, uncheckpointed and downloads every file twice, so a 2019–2026 top-100 run cannot finish in a working day and loses all progress when interrupted
bug.symptoms:
In _backfill_archive (bars_backfill.py ~line 1140), ranking walks all 752 candidates one at a time. For each one, _fetch_symbol_archive_rows downloads every monthly zip plus its .CHECKSUM, with DEFAULT_DELAY_SECONDS (0.2 s) after each request. That is roughly 37,000 files fetched sequentially.
Three things make this unworkable: - The rank cache (_save_rank_cache) is written only after the last candidate. An interruption at symbol 407 keeps nothing. - The candle rows fetched during ranking are discarded (`_rows`). The write phase then fetches the top-N symbols' files again. - The S3 listing (_list_archive_months) is redone on every run.
bug.reproduction_steps: With an injected fetch that counts calls and sleeps 10 ms per call, rank 30 synthetic symbols × 12 months: - Calls equal 2 × files during ranking, plus 2 × files again for the top-N writes. - Killing after 20 symbols and rerunning starts ranking at symbol 1.
bug.expected: - Verified file cache. - Every archive month that passes its checksum is written atomically (tmp then rename) to <LAKE>/staging-meta/archive-cache/<symbol>/<symbol>-1d-<YYYY-MM>.zip, together with its .CHECKSUM. - Any later need for that month, in ranking, in the write phase or in a rerun, reads the cached file and re-verifies its checksum, without a network call. - A cached file whose checksum fails is deleted and refetched. - The S3 listing is cached in <LAKE>/staging-meta/archive-listing.json and reused unless --restart is given. - The cache sits outside staging/, so it is never sealed. - Rank checkpoint. - Each ranked candidate's result (symbol, median volume, last archive month, or "unrankable") is appended as one JSON line to <LAKE>/staging-meta/rank-<window>.partial.jsonl as soon as it is known. - A rerun skips candidates already in the partial file. - Once all are done, the final rank cache is written and the partial file removed. - --restart ignores and clears all three: listing, partial rank and file cache. - Concurrency. - New --workers N, default 8, bounded to 1..32. It sets the number of candidates fetched in parallel with a thread pool. - Each worker keeps the per-request politeness delay. - An HTTP 429 or 418 response honours retry-after for that worker, as today. - The ranking, partitions, universe.json and every emitted summary are identical whatever the worker count. Ordering is by the existing sort key, never completion order. - Progress lines stay one per finished candidate, in completion order, with symbols_done increasing monotonically. - Expected scale: with --workers 8 and a warm cache, a rerun of the same window makes zero network calls until it reaches a month not yet cached. - test_backfill_rank_throughput.py, with an injected fetch over synthetic archive months that counts calls and needs no network, covers: - each month is fetched once across ranking and writing - an interrupted rank (the fetch raises after N symbols) resumes without refetching ranked symbols or cached months - --restart clears and refetches - a corrupted cached zip is detected, deleted and refetched - --workers 1 and --workers 8 produce byte-identical universe.json and partitions - 30 symbols × 12 months at 10 ms per call finish at least 4× faster with 8 workers than with 1 It passes under pytest-xdist.
bug.actual: Root cause: ranking is a single sequential loop with no incremental persistence, and fetched files are never kept, so the write phase and every rerun pay the full download again.
bug.constraints: The ranking rule (median daily quote volume over the window), the output layout and universe.json fields are unchanged The live REST source (--source rest) is unchanged No file outside the two listed is edited Do not edit docs/user-journeys/
